hook: Sebastien Bubeck trained in France, earning his PhD in mathematics at the University of Lille and receiving the Jacques Neveu prize for the best French doctoral thesis in probability and statistics. He worked as an assistant professor in Princeton University's Department of Operations Research and Financial Engineering before joining Microsoft Research in Redmond, where he leads work in the Machine Learning Foundations group and holds the title of Vice President and Distinguished Scientist. His early research centered on convex optimization and multi-armed bandit problems, work recognized with an Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship in 2015 and multiple best paper awards. He co-authored the 2015 monograph Convex Optimization: Algorithms and Complexity. His research focus shifted toward large language models, and in March 2023 he led the Microsoft Research team that wrote Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence, an early evaluation of GPT-4 that argued the model showed markedly more general capability than earlier systems. He also helped develop Microsoft's Phi family of small, efficiently trained language models.

standing.watch: What the records leave open is mostly the litigation. Both cases remain pending in discovery and consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143, with the consolidation recorded at 2026-09-24 and summary judgment briefing in the Times case closed April 2, 2026, so no outcome appears. The records name Microsoft and OpenAI in those matters, not Bubeck, so nothing indicates he is a party. The site lists no funding, valuation or financial figures for Microsoft beyond its founding year and location, and no listing, transaction or new venture involving him. Nothing in the records points to a change in his role at Microsoft Research or to a successor to the Phi or Sparks work. On these records, the next thing to resolve is the consolidated litigation, and beyond that the record is thin.
standing.record: The site's records on Bubeck are a profile, a set of quick facts, one company and two lawsuits. The company is Microsoft, where he is listed as an executive, a public company in Redmond, Washington, founded in 1975. The lawsuits are The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, in discovery with summary judgment briefing closed April 2, 2026, and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc., a class action in discovery, both consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143. Neither case names Bubeck personally in the records supplied, and neither is described as touching his own conduct. The pattern running through the record is a research career that moved from mathematical foundations, convex optimization and bandit problems, into the evaluation and development of large language models at Microsoft. The litigation attaches to the company and the models rather than to him, and the records offer no further detail on his part in either case.

achievements.title: Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence (2023)
achievements.impact: Led a Microsoft Research team analyzing an early version of GPT-4 and argued it showed markedly more general intelligence than prior models, a paper that shaped public and research debate over large language model capabilities.

achievements.title: Phi small language model family
achievements.impact: Helped develop Microsoft's Phi series of small, efficient language models, showing that carefully curated training data could let compact models rival much larger ones on many benchmarks.

achievements.title: Convex Optimization: Algorithms and Complexity (2015)
achievements.impact: Wrote a widely used monograph and course reference on modern convex optimization theory, adopted in graduate courses across the field.

achievements.title: Bandit convex optimization research
achievements.impact: Contributed foundational regret-bound results for stochastic and adversarial multi-armed bandit problems, work recognized with best paper awards at COLT, NeurIPS, and STOC.
